newsitem.title: USA: Staples posts record fourth quarter profits.
newsitem.headline: Staples posts record fourth quarter profits.

text.p: Staples Inc. Tuesday reported record sales and earnings for its fiscal fourth quarter as the office products superstore chain continued to grow at a rapid clip.

Staples, which is awaiting government approval for a $3.6 billion merger with rival Office Depot, Inc., said net income jumped 34 percent to $46.9 million, or 28 cents a share, in the quarter ended Feb. 1 from $34.9 million, or 21 cents a share, in the year-ago period.
Sales rose 19 percent to $1.2 billion from $975.5 million.
For the year, earnings surged to $106.4 million, or 64 cents a share, from $73.7 million, or 46 cents a share, in 1995. Sales rose 29 percent to $4.0 billion from $3.1 billion.
Comparable sales in Staples' 442 stores and delivery hubs that have been open for more than one year rose 11 percent for the quarter and 14 percent for the year.
Staples operates 574 office products superstores in over 100 markets in the United States and Canada under the names "Staples", "Staples Express", "Business Depot" and "Bureau En Gros."
A record 115 stores were opened and an additional 78 stores were remodeled to the company's new format in fiscal 1996. More than 80 percent of Staples' stores are either new or remodeled.
Staples stock rose 87.5 cents to $22.125 on Nasdaq. The earnings were released after the close of stock market trading.
